stem: (Select TWO.) Orchid Logistics commits `.terraform.lock.hcl` and wants every CI run, each starting from a fresh clone, to install the identical release of a registry module. Which two statements are accurate?

choices.text: The lock file records provider selections only, and it does not remember which module release was chosen
Running `terraform init -upgrade` in each CI job keeps the module on the release chosen the first time
Writing an exact `version = "6.0.1"` in the module block holds the module to that single release
A range such as `version = "~> 6.0"` keeps the first release installed on every later run
A `!=` condition in the constraint holds the module to a single release

rationale: At present the dependency lock file tracks only provider dependencies, and Terraform does not remember version selections for remote modules. The documented way to freeze a module is an exact version constraint, which always selects the same release. The upgrade flag does the opposite of holding a release: it moves modules to the newest release the constraint allows. A range constraint can move to a newer release the next time Terraform selects a version, and each fresh clone selects again because nothing remembers the first pick. The `!=` operator only excludes one exact version; it does not hold the module to a single release.
